title: Minimum size subarray sum
prompt:
PageTurn gives a "sprint" badge for the fewest consecutive days whose reading minutes add up to at least a goal.

Write minSubarrayLen(nums, goal) that returns the length of the shortest contiguous subarray of nums whose sum is >= goal, or 0 if there is none. All values are non-negative (that is what makes a sliding window safe). Aim for O(n) time.

Examples:

  • minSubarrayLen([10, 20, 5, 40, 15, 30], 55) → 2 (40 + 15)
  • minSubarrayLen([2, 3, 1, 2, 4, 3], 7) → 2 (4 + 3)
  • minSubarrayLen([1, 1, 1, 1], 11) → 0

Constraints: 0 ≤ nums.length ≤ 105, 0 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 104, 1 ≤ goal ≤ 109.

tests.name: a single element can be enough
must shrink more than once in a step
matches checking every subarray on many small inputs

hints: "Shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least X" with non-negative numbers is a variable sliding window, the "shortest" flavor.

Keep a running windowSum of nums[left..right]. Add nums[right] each step. Then, while windowSum >= goal, the window is a candidate: record right - left + 1, subtract nums[left] and move left forward to try a shorter one.

Shape:

let left = 0, windowSum = 0, best = Infinity;
for (let right = 0; right < nums.length; right++) {
  windowSum += nums[right];
  while (windowSum >= goal) {
    best = Math.min(best, right - left + 1);
    windowSum -= nums[left];
    left++;
  }
}
return best === Infinity ? 0 : best;
explain:
Time O(n), space O(1). right adds each element once and left removes each at most once. Trying every start is O(n²).

The window works only because the values are non-negative: adding an element never lowers the sum and removing one never raises it. With negative values you would switch to prefix sums.

In an interview: "Shortest contiguous run that reaches a target, all non-negative, so a sliding window: expand right, and while the sum reaches the goal, record the length and shrink from the left. Each element enters and leaves once, so O(n) time and O(1) space."
